close_reason: Fixed in 044b4f2: urgency and mention_urgency are now Option<UrgencyLevel> using the canonical impl_string_enum! pattern with Other(_) forward-compat. Wire-byte-equivalent.
description:
Trigger: a downstream consumer reads draft-atwood-jmap-chat-push-00 §4.1 and learns that urgency takes 'very-low' | 'low' | 'normal' | 'high'. They write ChatPushConfig { urgency: Some("hgih".to_owned()), .. } and the typo is not caught at compile time.

Bad behavior: crate-jmap-chat-types/src/push.rs:24-28 declares urgency: Option<String> and mention_urgency: Option<String>. The spec wire vocabulary is enumerable. The crate already uses impl_string_enum! for similar cases (ChatKind, DeliveryState, ReadDisposition, Presence) — each pairs a typed enum with an Other(String) forward-compat arm.

The string-typed declaration here:
- Lets typos pass compile and surface only as silently-ignored push config at runtime (server side does not validate; server discards unknown urgency strings).
- Diverges from the canonical-template pattern used elsewhere in this crate.
- Makes the ChatPushConfig wire docs less discoverable: a reader has to read the spec to learn the allowed values, instead of reading the rustdoc of an UrgencyLevel enum.

Fix: define UrgencyLevel as a string-enum with the four spec variants plus Other(String), update both fields. Non-breaking deserialize-wise — Other(String) absorbs anything not in the four. The break is on the Rust API but the crate is pre-1.0 and the type is #[non_exhaustive].

Priority P3 because the failure mode is 'config string silently ignored' rather than 'incorrect security decision', which is a reasonable real-world cost but not a P0/P1 footgun.
title: ChatPushConfig.urgency and mention_urgency: stringly-typed wire fields with enumerable wire vocab
